e-9821.knowledge_point: Calculating the Position Vector of a Particle Moving With Constant Velocity
e-9821.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(3\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{i}) \: \textrm{mi}$ with a constant velocity of $(\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}) \: \textrm{mi/h}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $2$ hours.
e-9821.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $\mathbf{u},$  the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{r}_0 + \mathbf{u} t,
$$

 
where $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
\mathbf{r}_0 = 3\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{i}, \qquad \mathbf u = \mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t = 2 \: \textrm{h}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(3j-i)+(i-j)(2) \\  & =(-i+3j)+(2i-2j) \\  & =(i+j)\,\text{mi}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9822.knowledge_point: Calculating the Position Vector of a Particle Moving With Constant Acceleration
e-9822.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(4\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j})\,\textrm{cm}$ with an acceleration of $(\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{cm/min}^2$ and an initial velocity of $(\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}) \: \textrm{cm/min}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $4$ minutes.
e-9822.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $\mathbf{a},$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{r}_0 + \mathbf{u} t + \dfrac12 \mathbf{a} t^2,
$$

 

where $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the initial position of the particle and $\mathbf{u}$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
\mathbf{r}_0 = 4\mathbf i - \mathbf j , \qquad \mathbf u = \mathbf{i} +\mathbf{j}, \qquad \mathbf a = \mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t = 4 \, \textrm{min}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(4i-j)+(i+j)(4)+\frac{1}{2}(i+3j)(4)^{2} \\  & =(4i-j)+(4i+4j)+8(i+3j) \\  & =(8i+3j)+(8i+24j) \\  & =(16i+27j)\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-9824.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Particle and the Origin
e-9824.problem: A particle moves from the origin with an acceleration of $(\mathbf{i} +\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{cm/s}^2$ and an initial velocity of $(-\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}) \: \textrm{cm/s}.$ Find the distance from the particle to the origin after $6$ seconds.
e-9824.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $\mathbf{a},$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{r}_0 + \mathbf{u} t + \dfrac12 \mathbf{a} t^2,
$$

 

where $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the initial position of the particle and $\mathbf{u}$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
\mathbf{r}_0 = 0\mathbf i +0 \mathbf j , \qquad \mathbf u = -\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}, \qquad \mathbf a = \mathbf{i} +\mathbf{j}.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t = 6 \, \textrm{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(0i+0j)+(-i-2j)(6)+\frac{1}{2}(i+j)(6)^{2} \\  & =(-6i-12j)+18(i+j) \\  & =(-6i-12j)+(18i+18j) \\  & =(12i+6j)\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance from the particle to the origin at this time is

$$
\begin{aligned}|r| & =|12i+6j| \\  & =\sqrt{{12}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144+36} \\  & =\sqrt{180} \\  & =6\sqrt{5}\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(i-4j)\,\text{km}$ with a constant velocity of $i\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $2$ hours.
after.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $u,$  the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut,
$$

 
where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=i-4j,\,u=i.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=2\,\text{h}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(i-4j)+i(2) \\  & =(i-4j)+2i \\  & =(3i-4j)\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$

A particle starts moving from the point with position vector −2jft with an acceleration of 4ift/min2 and an initial velocity of (3i+j)ft/min. Find the position vector of the particle after 2 minutes.

a
(−7i−14j)ft
b
14ift
c
(5i−j)ft
d
−7jft
e
(15i+5j)ft
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

If a particle moves with constant acceleration a, the position vector of the particle at time t can be found using

r=r0+ut+12at2,

where r0 is the initial position of the particle and u is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have r0=−2j,u=3i+j,a=4i.

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after t=2min is r=(−2j)+(3i+j)(2)+12(4i)(2)2=−2j+(6i+2j)+2(4i)=6i+8i=14ift.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms r = −2j + 2(3i+j) + ½(4i)(2²) = 14i ft. Thus option b is correct.

content.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $-2j\,\text{ft}$ with an acceleration of $4i\,{\text{ft/min}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(3i+j)\,\text{ft/min}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $2$ minutes.
content.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=-2j,\,u=3i+j,\,a=4i.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=2\,\text{min}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(-2j)+(3i+j)(2)+\frac{1}{2}(4i)(2)^{2} \\  & =-2j+(6i+2j)+2(4i) \\  & =6i+8i \\  & =14i\,\text{ft}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(-i+j)\,\text{mm}$ with an acceleration of $(2i-6j)\,{\text{mm/min}}^{2}$ and an initial velocity of $(-3i+2j)\,\text{mm/min}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $5$ minutes.
after.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant acceleration $a,$ the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut+\frac{1}{2}a{t}^{2},
$$

 

where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle and $u$ is its initial velocity.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=-i+j,\,u=-3i+2j,\,a=2i-6j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=5\,\text{min}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =(-i+j)+(-3i+2j)(5)+\frac{1}{2}(2i-6j)(5)^{2} \\  & =(-i+j)+(-15i+10j)+25(i-3j) \\  & =(-16i+11j)+(25i-75j) \\  & =(9i-64j)\,\text{mm}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
